Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(-2)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$

${h}^{′}(-2)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(-2)=\frac{{f}^{′}(-2)\cdot g(-2)-f(-2)\cdot {g}^{′}(-2)}{(g(-2))^{2}}.
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(-2)=3$ and $g(-2)=2.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-3,-1)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-2)=-1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (-3,-1)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${g}^{′}(-2)=-1.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(-2) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-2)\cdot g(-2)-f(-2)\cdot {g}^{′}(-2)}{(g(-2))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 2-3\cdot (-1)}{(2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
